thread.title: Nikkei rises as Kuroda renominated to lead Bank of Japan

author: Suryatapa Bhattacharya
title: Nikkei rises as Kuroda renominated to lead Bank of Japan
text:
Stocks in Japan, Australia and New Zealand gained Friday, while a number of major markets were closed for the   as investors regained confidence in equities after sharp slides last week.
Taking cues from another robust session on Wall Street overnight, Japan’s Nikkei Stock Exchange NIK, +1.16% led gains in Asia, rising 1.2%, despite a stronger yen.
And as expected, Gov. Haruhiko Kuroda was nominated to lead the Bank of Japan for a second term.
The markets that are open took their cues from improving investor sentiment this week and gains in global stocks overnight.
The Dow   above 25,000 for the first time since Feb. 2, with market participants expressing greater comfort about the prospect of higher U.S. inflation and Treasury yields.
Japanese technology stocks tracked the gains of U.S. counterparts, including Apple AAPL, +3.36% , overnight. Kyocera was higher 3.9% and Sony 6758, +1.80% gained 3%.
Japan’s car makers were also higher despite the stronger yen. Honda Motor 7267, +0.99% was up 1.9%, Toyota Motor 7203, +1.29% added 1.2% and Nissan Motor 7201, +0.36% gained 1.1%.
The dollar JPYUSD, +0.347025% was trading at ¥106.22 having fallen to ¥106.01 earlier in the morning, its lowest point since November 2016, prompting a response from Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso.
“Stability of foreign exchange rates is important, and there is no change in the government’s stance that it will take appropriate action at the appropriate time, if needed,” he said, escalating his language from a day earlier.
In addition to Kuroda’s renomination, the Japanese government also nominated Masazumi Wakatabe and Masayoshi Amamiya for deputy governor positions at the central bank. Amamiya is a career BOJ official. Wakatabe is a professor at Waseda University and is viewed as an advocate of radical easing.
“[Market participants] want to see how monetary policy stance is set to change under the new deputies in [Mr.] Kuroda’s second term,” said Hiroki Shimazu, chief strategist at MCP Inc.
In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 XJO, -0.08% was up 0.1%, building on yesterday’s rebound with broad gains in industrial, health care and bank stocks. The index is on track for a 1.5% rebound this week after tumbling 4.6% last week.
New Zealand’s shares NZ50GR, +0.77% were up 0.5%, helped by a strong rise from one of its biggest stocks. Auckland International Airport AIA, +2.78% was about 3% higher after saying its first-half profit was higher while narrowing its earnings guidance for the fiscal year. Friday’s gains come despite further losses for Fletcher Building FBU, +0.57% , taking its slide this week to about 11%. The solid gains for the NZX 50 come after the index reached a three-month low earlier in the week.
